en: The Vajradevīstotra composed by Ācārya Nāgārjuna. Om, homage to the illustrious Goddess Yoginī.
The Ḍākinī, who is all the Buddhas, the remover of all fears, the pervasive Mother of the Universe—
she has one face, is red in color, and is delighted by her three eyes; she is the most excellent beauty among the Khecarīs,
blazing with a divine body, having placed her feet in the sky, possessing two arms, and having loose, flowing hair.
Holding a khaṭvāṅga in her left hand and a trident (śakti) in her right hand, she possesses a celestial form. || 1 ||

Naked-bodied, with a garland around her neck and adorned with human heads, she possesses the five mudrās as ornaments; she grants the supreme boon of the path to liberation for sentient beings and bestows the accomplishment of primordial wisdom.
(She is) the Śrī Devī who protects living beings and brings benefit to the world—the Yoginī Vajradīpti.
O Queen of the Vidyādharīs, I bow my head in prostration and praise your lotus-like feet.
The Blessed Great Goddess is your refuge, O Vajra;
I constantly worship your lotus feet, I honor you—be gracious to me. (3)
You alone are the mother of all Buddhas, the bestower of enlightenment;
you are the mother of all Bodhisattvas, who protects their welfare.
She who gathers all that is for the benefit and welfare [of beings], she who purifies all sins, who agitates the hosts of wicked Māras, and who bestows the bliss of great joy. (5)

Bestowing the qualities of power and vigor for the exertion in accomplishing the true Dharma, she grants the bliss of meditative absorption and concentration, which is tranquil and free from afflictions. || 6 ||
Bestowing the abundant glory of the great jewel of the qualities of wisdom, I take refuge in and worship the lotus feet of the Blessed Lady. (7)
I pay homage to Vajravārāhī, who liberates one from all sins;
to the Goddess who destroys the Māras and bestows the fruit of Buddhahood. (8)
I bow to the glorious Vajravārāhī, the sovereign of Jinas whose very form is mantra;
to the goddess who grants supreme boons and bestows the excellence of supernatural powers and accomplishments. (9)
I praise you, O Mistress of the Thunderbolt, born from the family of Vairocana, with disheveled hair and three eyes, possessing the hue of twilight and vermilion. 10.
I bow to Vajravilāsinī, who is adorned with the beauty of the five mudrās upon her head, who carries a khaṭvāṅga on her shoulder, and who holds a vajra and a skull-cup in her hands.
I salute Trailokyasundarī, who bears the five mudrās upon her body, adorned with a garland of severed heads, and whose lotus-face bears a playful smile. 12.

I bow to her who is preceded by Bhairava, who has three faces, whose throat is powerful, who is Carcikā, who is intensely fierce and terrible for the purpose of inciting hatred, and who is fearsome and awe-inspiring.
I bow to that Goddess Jñānaḍākinī, who is born between passion and dispassion, eternally free from the fragments of existence and non-existence. 14.

I bow to you, who are worshipped by the gods, who constantly delight in drinking the five nectars and wine, who enjoy the excellent food of the five grains, and who are ever devoted to song and instrumental music. 15.
I salute her who is eternally the innate bliss, the perpetual one, the abode of all; she whose anklets jingle as she is devoted to the dance. 16.
I pay homage to you, the Goddess, the bestower of accomplishments, the eternal consort of the practitioners of yoga, the giver of the Buddha’s nirvāṇa—the Mother of the Buddha. (17)
I bow to Vajrayoginī, whose limbs are red, who possesses a divine form by nature, the compassionate goddess who has taken a transcendent body. 18.
I bow to Vajrayoginī, the Queen of Jinas, who resembles the bandhūka flower, whose form is peaceful, and who bestows supernatural powers and accomplishments. (19)
I bow to Vajrayoginī, the goddess who pervades the three worlds, appearing as a twelve-year-old maiden with the form of a fresh dancer. (20)
The Vajradevīstotra, composed by the venerable master Ācārya Nāgārjuna, is completed.
